                [32m"- Implement a small HTTP API on top of `rwsdk`'s router that uploads, retrieves, lists, and deletes objects from that bucket. All endpoints must be served by the same `rwsdk` worker.\n"[39m +
                [32m'- Object keys must be derived from the SHA-256 hash of the uploaded bytes so the same file always maps to the same key.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The API must support the following endpoints (all responses are JSON unless noted):\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - **`POST /api/files`**\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - Request: `multipart/form-data` with a single `file` field.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - Behavior: Stores the file in R2 under key `uploads/<sha256-hex-of-bytes>.<ext>`, where:\n'[39m +
                [32m'      - `<sha256-hex-of-bytes>` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the raw file bytes.\n'[39m +
                [32m"      - `<ext>` is the original file's extension (without the dot), inferred from the uploaded filename. If the filename has no extension, the key has no `.<ext>` suffix (i.e. `uploads/<sha256-hex-of-bytes>`).\n"[39m +
                [32m'    - Response: HTTP `201`, JSON body:\n'[39m +
                [32m'      ```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'      {\n'[39m +
                [32m'        "key": "uploads/<sha256-hex>.<ext>",\n'[39m +
                [32m'        "size": <integer-bytes>,\n'[39m +
                [32m'        "contentType": "<original-content-type>",\n'[39m +
                [32m'        "sha256": "<sha256-hex>"\n'[39m +
                [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                [32m'      ```\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - Re-uploading the same bytes (same content) must yield the same `key` and `sha256`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - If no `file` field is present, return HTTP `400`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - **`GET /api/files/:key`**\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - `:key` is the full R2 key, URL-encoded (e.g. `uploads%2F<sha>.<ext>`).\n'[39m +
                [32m"    - On success: HTTP `200`, raw response body equal to the stored bytes, with `Content-Type` set to the original upload's content type and `Content-Length` set to the stored size.\n"[39m +
                [32m'    - If the key does not exist: HTTP `404`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - **`DELETE /api/files/:key`**\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - URL-encoded `:key` as above.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - On success (key existed and was deleted): HTTP `204`, empty body.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - If the key does not exist: HTTP `404`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - **`GET /api/files`**\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - Lists every object under the `uploads/` prefix.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    - Response: HTTP `200`, JSON body:\n'[39m +
                [32m'      ```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'      {\n'[39m +
                [32m'        "objects": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'          { "key": "uploads/...", "size": <integer-bytes>, "uploaded": "<ISO-8601-timestamp>" }\n'[39m +
                [32m'        ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                [32m'      ```\n'[39m +
                [32m"      `objects` MUST be an array (possibly empty). Each entry's `uploaded` must be a valid ISO-8601 string.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Use the standard `rwsdk/worker` `defineApp` + `rwsdk/router` `route` primitives. The R2 binding is reachable via `env.BUCKET` (import `env` from `cloudflare:workers`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The `R2Bucket` API (`put`, `get`, `delete`, `list`) is the standard Cloudflare Workers R2 API.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The default dev server runs on Vite — start it bound to port `5173` on all interfaces (`0.0.0.0`) so it is reachable from outside the dev container.'[39m
            }
          ]

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. EXPECTED MATCHES: If you want to replace multiple instances:\n'[39m +

            [32m"   - If the actual number of matches doesn't equal expectedReplacements, the edit will fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'   - This is a safety feature to prevent unintended replacements\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. VERIFICATION: Before using this tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Command Execution:\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +

            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.\n'[39m +
            [32m'It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## When to Use This Tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions\n'[39m +

            [32m'## Task States and Management\n'[39m +
